summary: A type-checker soundness bug where zero-length array constants of type `!` incorrectly mark subsequent code as unreachable; needs an inline story with low-level design and test cases.

steps.why: Single-repo compiler bug needs clear requirements with acceptance criteria for the fix.
steps.instructions: Focus on the type-checker's treatment of `!`-typed constants in zero-length array contexts; the divergence analysis must not affect reachability when the constant is never evaluated.

steps.why: Compiler bug fix needs concrete file plan identifying affected type-checking and MIR generation code paths.
steps.instructions: Identify the type-checking phase that incorrectly propagates divergence from unevaluated constants, and the MIR lowering that marks subsequent code unreachable; include safeguards to prevent similar issues.

steps.why: Soundness bug with multiple manifestations needs comprehensive test coverage including the provided examples and edge cases.
steps.instructions: Cover both the trait-based and direct `[!; 0]` patterns; test debug and release builds; verify no SIGILL and correct runtime behavior when bounds check fails.

steps.why: Human approval of specs and this plan before Dev.

skipped.why: Single inline story with no cross-artifact dependencies to check.
